internal_discovery.plain_explanation: Across all 12 occurrences the root marks the bad end of a person's lot: being wretched, hard-pressed, or ill-fated, as opposed to being fortunate and at ease (سعيد). The Qur'an itself sets the opposite pole (11:105 pairs شَقِىّ with سَعِيد). What KIND of misfortune it is comes from the surrounding words, not the root: physical toil and want when Adam is warned of leaving the Garden (20:117, glossed by 20:118-119 hunger/thirst/nakedness/heat) and when the Prophet is told the Qur'an was not sent 'to distress you' (20:2); the wretched who reach the Fire (11:106, and the superlative 'most-wretched' at 92:15/87:11); an ingrained wretched-state (23:106 شِقْوَة); a graceless character coupled with tyranny (19:32 جَبَّار شَقِيّ); and being 'left empty-handed' in prayer (19:4, 19:48). The last of these is a fixed twice-used idiom carrying specific 'fruitless-supplication' content the bare root does not supply, which is why the account cannot be graded above MODERATE.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: Does NOT lexically mean 'damnation/Fire' — the Fire is added by explicit فِى ٱلنَّارِ / يَصْلَىٰهَا (11:106, 92:15), never by the root (20:2 uses the same verb for the faultless Prophet). Does NOT entail sin/disobedience — it names the adverse condition/lot, not the wrong act; moral shading at 19:32/91:12 comes from coordination (جَبَّار) and narrative, not the root. Is NOT synonymous with ضلال — 20:123 lists لَا يَضِلُّ / وَلَا يَشْقَىٰ as two distinct averted outcomes, and 23:106 pairs شِقْوَة with a separate ضَآلِّين. Is NEVER neutral or positive — no occurrence of rewarded/productive toil; it is always privation/affliction, excluding a mere 'effort/labour' reading. Not restricted by subject: applies to a favoured prophet (20:2), a group-worst individual (91:12), whole classes (11:105-106), and an abstract state (23:106).
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: 20:2 لِتَشْقَىٰ is addressed to the Prophet as this-worldly burden/distress with no moral fault and no Fire, disproving any damnation/wickedness nucleus; the eschatological content in 11:106/92:15 is supplied by explicit فِى ٱلنَّارِ / يَصْلَىٰهَا, not by the root. Symmetrically, forcing a 'mere physical toil' gloss breaks on 11:105 (↔ سَعِيد) and 92:15 (ٱلْأَشْقَى + burning). This two-sided pressure is what forces the broad adverse-lot nucleus rather than either narrow pole.
internal_discovery.strongest_competitor: A poly-class / two-lexeme reading sharing only negative valence: (i) experiential worldly toil-hardship (20:2, 20:117, 20:123), (ii) the wretched/doomed end-state (11:105, 11:106, 23:106, 87:11, 91:12, 92:15), and (iii) the دعاء idiom 'disappointed supplicant' (19:4, 19:48). It has surface appeal because elatives/masdar cluster eschatological and the Ṭā-Hā verbs cluster experiential. It FAILS as a clean split because the morphology-to-sense mapping is not bounded (11:106 شَقُوا۟ is a VERB that is eschatological, while 19:4/19:48 شَقِيًّا are the فعيل form yet experiential), and the classes are bridged by the shared 'loss of the good' pole plus the single سعيد antonym — so they are contextual instantiations of one nucleus, not unbridged lexemes. But because the unity is only a shared abstract pole (not a demonstrated single semantic operation), the competitor legitimately caps confidence.

internal_discovery.rationale: All three lenses converge on a single adverse-lot / negative-pole nucleus anchored verse-internally to سعيد (11:105) and bridged within one sura/narrative frame by 20:117 (Garden-loss = hardship) and 20:123 (guidance ⇒ neither astray nor wretched). Hence PREFERRED, not UNRESOLVED: there IS a Quran-internal bridge, so a forced multi-class split is not warranted. Scope is REPRESENTATIVE (DERIVATIONAL_FAMILY) because the claim spans V / فعيل / أَفْعَل-elative / فِعْلة with the domain context-supplied rather than universally-established distinctiveness. Strength is MODERATE, not STRONG: (1) a coherent, twice-attested, semi-lexicalized resistant sub-class — بِدُعَآء … شَقِيًّا (19:4, 19:48), predicated of prophets, carrying 'fruitless-prayer' content the root does not itself supply and bridging to the wretched pole only interpretively; per contract a resistant lexicalized sub-class caps strength at MODERATE; (2) the unifying nucleus is thin/valence-level and anchors two different antonym axes (↔ سَعِيد at 11:105 and ↔ ٱلْأَتْقَى at 92:15/17), edging toward a fits-everything abstraction; (3) a clean domain-splitting counterexample (20:2 fault-free vs 11:106 Fire); (4) small sample (n=12) with the eschatological sub-use externally supplied. Lens B argued STRONG but its own honest fallback was MODERATE; two of three lenses grade MODERATE and the contract's resistant-lexicalized-class rule is decisive. Grade: MODERATE / REPRESENTATIVE.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Form-I stative verb 'to be/become in an adverse lot — to fall into hardship, distress, or wretched ill-being.' Domain runs from faultless worldly toil/want (20:2 Prophet; 20:117 Adam, glossed by 20:118-119) through the guidance-averted misery of 20:123 to the eschatological wretched who reach the Fire (11:106, via explicit فِى ٱلنَّارِ).
clusters.classification_rationale: All four are base Form-I (qac_verb_form null, qac_pos V) and share the negative-pole nucleus; the eschatological reading at 11:106 is contributed by فِى ٱلنَّارِ, not the verb, and 20:2/20:117 carry zero moral/otherworldly load — proving the root under-specifies domain.
clusters.supporting_evidence_note: 20:123 لَا يَضِلُّ وَلَا يَشْقَىٰ separates the root from ضلال; 20:117→20:118-119 glosses شقاء as hunger/thirst/nakedness/heat (loss of eased lot).

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: فَعِيل شَقِيّ as a personal descriptor for one on the adverse/wretched pole: 11:105 fixes the pole antonymically (شَقِىّ ↔ سَعِيد); 19:32 colours character (a graceless wretch coupled with جَبَّار 'tyrant,' opposed to بَرّ).
clusters.classification_rationale: Same فعيل form; 11:105 is the decisive antonym control anchoring the whole root, and 19:32 extends the pole to disposition (embodying badness) rather than a suffered condition — a wider but bridged edge of the same nucleus.
clusters.supporting_evidence_note: 11:105 فَمِنْهُمْ شَقِىٌّ وَسَعِيدٌ is the internal opposition that defines شقي as the negative counter-pole of سعيد. QAC tags this شَقِىّ as N and the identical شَقِيًّا as ADJ at 19:32 — morphology does not track meaning here.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: أَفْعَل elative 'the most-wretched / most ill-fated one' — a superlative of the same pole. 92:15 لَا يَصْلَىٰهَآ إِلَّا ٱلْأَشْقَى (↔ ٱلْأَتْقَى 92:17); 87:11 وَيَتَجَنَّبُهَا ٱلْأَشْقَى; 91:12 the Thamud individual.
clusters.classification_rationale: Transparent superlatives of the wretched pole; 92:15's pairing with ٱلْأَتْقَى confirms the pole is Quran-internally fixed. 91:12 attaches the label to an individual by adverse standing.
clusters.supporting_evidence_note: 91:12 أَشْقَىٰهَا labels the Thamud perpetrator who actively hamstrings the she-camel — an agent of evil, not one visibly suffering — so the elative shades 'wretched' toward 'most-ruined/most-wicked' titularly rather than a suffered condition; bridgeable (his wretchedness = his ruin/doom) but the point of a mild moral-agent strain.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: فِعْلة شِقْوَة — the abstract ingrained state/propensity of wretchedness: 'our شِقْوَة overcame us,' co-listed with yet distinct from ضلال (ضَآلِّين).
clusters.classification_rationale: Abstract nominalization of the same negative pole; its co-listing with ضَآلِّين reinforces the ش ق و ≠ ضلال boundary.

resistant_deep_analysis.preliminary_note: The twice-attested collocation بِدُعَآء … شَقِيًّا (19:4 Zachariah, 19:48 Abraham) predicates the root of prophets as 'deprived/left empty-handed in supplication,' a coherent semi-lexicalized sub-class whose 'fruitless-prayer' content is not supplied by the root and bridges to the wretched-pole only interpretively — capping strength at MODERATE. It is not derivable from the toil or damnation domains without an interpretive leap, and being predicated of prophets it is the antithesis of the doomed class.

independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A, B, C) all affirm the single negative-pole nucleus; two of three (A, C) independently grade MODERATE and identify the same resistant material (19:4/19:48 دعاء seam; 20:2 vs 11:106 domain split), and B's own honest fallback is MODERATE.
candidate_root_contribution: ش ق و = to be or become in the NEGATIVE POLE of one's condition — badly-off, hard-pressed, wretched, ill-fated: the privation of ease/wellbeing, the explicit counter-pole of سعادة/سعيد (fixed verse-internally at 11:105 شَقِىّ ↔ سَعِيد). The root is uniformly negative-valenced and supplies only this adverse-lot nucleus; the DOMAIN of the privation — worldly toil/want, settled eschatological ruin, unanswered supplication, or graceless character — is supplied by context/collocation, not by the root itself.

layer_attribution.occurrence_evidence: 12/12 occurrences read in-packet: 4 Form-I verbs (11:106, 20:2, 20:117, 20:123), 4 فَعِيل شَقِيّ/شَقِيًّا (11:105, 19:4, 19:32, 19:48), 3 أَفْعَل elatives (87:11, 91:12, 92:15), 1 فِعْلة masdar شِقْوَة (23:106); verse_texts and word_refs confirmed against the packet.
layer_attribution.derivation: One derivational family off ش ق و: base Form-I stative verb, the فَعِيل personal descriptor, the أَفْعَل elative superlative, and the فِعْلة abstract-state masdar — all instantiating the same negative-pole nucleus; QAC N/ADJ tags do not track meaning (identical شَقِيًّا tagged N at 19:4 and ADJ at 19:32/19:48).
layer_attribution.lexical_class: A semi-lexicalized sub-class exists: the fixed collocation بِدُعَآء … شَقِيًّا (19:4, 19:48) = 'deprived/empty-handed in supplication,' carrying specific fruitless-prayer content not supplied by the bare root; this is the resistant seam that caps the grade at MODERATE.
layer_attribution.contextual_relation: Domain of the privation is contextual, not root-borne: Fire via فِى ٱلنَّارِ / يَصْلَىٰهَا (11:106, 92:15), Garden-loss/want via 20:117→20:118-119, tyranny-coupling via جَبَّار (19:32), the perpetrator narrative (91:12), and the دعاء frame (19:4/19:48). This contextual/narrative meaning must NOT be read into the root claim, which remains the generic adverse/negative pole.
layer_attribution.reconciliation: No preliminary→final disposition flips were required; lens disagreement was on strength only (B=STRONG vs A/C=MODERATE), resolved to MODERATE by the contract rule that a coherent resistant lexicalized sub-class (the دعاء seam) caps strength at MODERATE + REPRESENTATIVE, consistent with B's own stated fallback.
layer_attribution.unresolved_resistance: The دعاء sub-class (19:4, 19:48) persists as a recorded RESISTANT seam bridged only interpretively to the wretched pole; the nucleus's thinness (anchoring both the سعيد happiness-axis and the أتقى piety-axis) leaves distinctiveness not fully established. Neither is severe enough to force an UNRESOLVED multi-class result, since a genuine Quran-internal bridge (11:105 ↔ سعيد; 20:117; 20:123) holds the classes together.

Each hard case is evidence-derived, and its statement also appears in the strongest_counterexample or the relevant cluster note.

rejection_condition.challenging_finding: A Quran-internal occurrence where ش ق و carries a positively-valenced or purely neutral 'effort/labour' sense, or where the root INHERENTLY (not via added context like فِى ٱلنَّارِ or the دعاء frame) fixes a single specific domain (e.g. damnation) that cannot be read as the generic adverse/negative pole opposed to سعيد.
rejection_condition.search_location: Re-examine the domain-carriers 11:106 (فِى ٱلنَّارِ), 92:15/87:11 (elatives), and the دعاء pair 19:4/19:48, plus the faultless uses 20:2/20:117, testing whether the specific content is root-supplied or context-supplied.
rejection_condition.verification_method: For each occurrence strip the collocational carrier and test whether the bare root still resolves to 'negative pole of one's condition'; check the antonym field (سعيد 11:105, أتقى 92:15/17) for any positive/neutral usage of the root.
rejection_condition.confounder_control: Ignore QAC N/ADJ tag noise (identical شَقِيًّا tagged both ways at 19:4 vs 19:32/19:48); do not import classical-lexicon 'toil' vs 'damnation' priors; distinguish content the root supplies from content the verse frame (Fire, Garden, دعاء) supplies.
rejection_condition.failure_consequence: If a positive/neutral use or a genuinely root-supplied fixed domain is found, the uniform-negative-pole nucleus is falsified and the result must be downgraded to WEAK or split into a multi-class UNRESOLVED account.

reopen_conditions: If a segment-level Arabic alignment or corrected morphology reclassifies شَقُوا۟ (11:106) or the تَشْقَىٰ verbs (20:2, 20:117, 20:123) such that the verbal class no longer shares the نnegative-pole nucleus with the فعيل/elative nominals, re-test the verb↔nominal bridge.

If additional occurrences of the collocation بِدُعَآء … شَقِيًّا beyond 19:4/19:48 appear, or if that idiom is shown to be productive rather than fixed, re-assess whether the دعاء sub-class should be promoted from RESISTANT seam to its own LEXICALIZED_CLASS or force an UNRESOLVED multi-class result.
If any occurrence is found where the root is positively/neutrally valenced (e.g. rewarded toil), reopen the 'uniformly negative pole' nucleus and the ≠effort/labour boundary.

falsification_evidence.status_rationale: A clean adversarial refutation returning SUPPORTED with distinctiveness_ok=true and failing_occurrences=[] cannot be claimed: the unifying nucleus is thin/valence-level (anchoring two antonym axes, سعيد and أتقى) so distinctiveness is not established, and the دعاء sub-class (19:4/19:48) resists as a semi-lexicalized seam. The core adverse-lot pole nonetheless holds across all 12 with a real Quran-internal bridge (11:105, 20:117, 20:123). Per contract, when some occurrences resist but the core holds, falsification is NOT_RUN and the resistant occurrences are recorded.
